Import a public compute shader

Start with a compute shader that reads and writes independent buffer elements. Add its source to shdr_target_shaders, bind its declared resources by name, and run the resulting pipeline on the CPU or a compatible GPU. An existing .comp extension is accepted. The build embeds the portable GPU variant directly in the application.

Use a unique identifier-shaped source basename in each linked target, such as multiply.comp or filter.cpp. The CMake helper derives its factory name from that basename. Each basename identifies one factory within the target.

Backend compatibility depends on buffer layout, builtins, extensions and synchronization. Consult the supported language subset before importing shared workgroup memory, atomics, samplers or custom records.

A mutable global with an explicit initializer starts from that value for every invocation on both backends. Each invocation receives independent private global storage. Put shared or persistent data in a bound buffer or image, and assign uninitialized private variables before reading them.

What these checks establish

The selected inputs cover complete compute programs, compiler conformance fixtures and support units. Reference acceptance means that the original input compiled and linked in OpenGL mode, or compiled to Vulkan SPIR-V when its declarations required Vulkan. CPU translation covers inputs accepted by at least one reference mode. Every record retains both reference outcomes.

Checked-in reference transcripts identify upstream fixtures with expected compiler diagnostics. This metadata and the standalone compiler result describe their respective test configurations. Every source record preserves the original expectation flag.

Compiler coverage. Successful exports establish compiler compatibility with the five language profiles. Applications supply the host resources, dimensions and valid input domains for runtime execution. Bundled runtime examples measure CPU/GPU agreement against independent references on the listed devices.

Devices must also support the imported resource counts, workgroup sizes and input dimensions. The bundled runtime examples separately compare CPU and GPU values, including independent numerical references. Inspect each record and validate an imported kernel with its intended inputs before deployment.

Source assembly and portable imports

NCNN sources depend on host-supplied types and load/store macros. The verifier inserts the exact pinned src/ncnn_glsl_ext.comp prelude and records the FP32 buffer configuration. This configuration uses FP32 buffer storage. The records retain the shared-memory paths selected by NCNN_shader_local_memory=1 and their compiler diagnostics. Upstream activation includes are resolved by glslang before CPU translation. The upstream body remains unchanged. Configuration, prelude, configured-source and preprocessed-source hashes are shown in the affected records.

The adapter selects a version, assigns buffer bindings and layouts, maps descriptor set zero and specialization defaults, and exposes supported push-constant members as named uniforms. The portable GPU variant supplies numeric promotions required by GLSL ES, removes local const qualifiers from runtime initializers, and handles integer boolean-selector mix on older profiles. It preserves expression evaluation order and keeps output and input-output arguments as lvalues. Global and compile-time local constants retain their qualifiers. These imports use the OpenGL resource and dispatch API.

The dual-backend subset covers independent invocations, single-array storage blocks, fixed local arrays, documented storage images and math operations. The detailed records identify requirements involving workgroup coordination, atomics, multi-field storage blocks, additional image formats, samplers, subgroups, cooperative matrices and reduced-precision types through their compiler diagnostics.

Reproduce the compiler checks

Use Python 3.8 or newer, Git, a C++11 compiler and glslangValidator. The commands below fetch pinned inputs explicitly into a separate cache.

# Fetch the pinned collection into a separate cache and write a standalone report.
python3 scripts/verify_public_shaders.py --fetch \
  --cache build/public-shaders --output build/public-shader-results.html
# Reuse the prepared local cache.
python3 scripts/verify_public_shaders.py \
  --cache build/public-shaders --output build/public-shader-results.html

A build configured with glslang also provides cmake --build build --target verify_public_shaders. Populate its cache first. The --jobs, --cxx and --glslang options select parallelism and tools. Each report records fingerprints for the implementation held constant throughout verification.

Fetch the upstream sources with the command above and follow their licenses when incorporating them. Every repository pin, source link and license link is retained below.
